# The Economic Machine

A single-page React investment diagnostic dashboard modeled on Bridgewater
Associates' systematic macro framework, rendered in a neoclassical design
language — Greek-revival restraint, stone panels, and a strong central axis.

Everything is driven by two state variables — **growth surprise** and
**inflation surprise**, each in σ units — generated by a seeded PRNG so every
session is reproducible. There is no backend.

## Sections

| § | Module | What it does |
|---|--------|--------------|
| I | The Machine | SVG macro compass (2×2 regime quadrants with a dotted trail), the Three Gears (productivity, short- and long-term debt cycles), and the release tape (priced-in vs actual vs surprise) |
| II | Beta — All Weather | Risk-parity sleeves: four seasons at 25% risk each vs the 60/40 capital illusion, dual capital/risk bars |
| III | Alpha — Pure Alpha | Six IF/THEN macro principles evaluated live against the surprises; FIRED or dormant |
| IV | The Register | Fifteen liquid holdings scored `βG·g + βI·i + carry + (ER − cash)/10` and re-ranked into five tiers on every release; checkboxes elect the working portfolio |
| V | Monte Carlo | 400 GBM paths × 40 quarters for the elected equal-weight book; percentile fan chart and terminal-value table |
| VI | Returns Ledger | Analytic CAGR / vol / Sharpe / lognormal 10-yr HPR (median & 5th pct) per elected holding |
| VII | Safeguards | Risk-of-ruin monitor with a 2.5% ceiling; breaching it engages a full-width hardstop banner |

An optional **Fetch Live Macro Data** control calls the Anthropic Messages API
(with the web-search tool) directly from the browser to pull the latest US GDP,
core CPI, and policy-rate prints, converts them to surprise σ, and pushes them
onto the compass trail. Any failure falls back gracefully to simulation with a
visible status line. Bring your own API key; it is held in component state only.

## Running

```sh
npm install
npm run dev       # http://localhost:5173
npm run build     # production build to dist/
npm run preview   # serve the production build
```

Fonts are self-hosted in `public/fonts/` (latin subsets of Playfair Display,
Source Serif 4, and IBM Plex Mono), so the page has no external runtime
dependencies.

## Disclaimer

All expected returns, volatilities, betas, and carry figures are model
assumptions for illustration. Nothing here is investment advice.
